title: Daniel Palacios

title: Daniel Palacios
text:
About
Daniel Palacios is an applied AI research scientist and PhD candidate in Quantitative & Computational Biosciences at Baylor College of Medicine, advised by Dr. Zhandong Liu in the Liu Lab at the Data Science Center, Texas Children’s Hospital. He builds AI systems that turn messy, real-world clinical data into answers clinicians and researchers can use.
Most of his work is where large language models meet electronic health records. Clinical data is split between structured tables and free-text notes, and the questions that matter rarely fit a single model. He approaches this from several angles:

Prediction: agentic and multi-agent LLM systems that plan, code, debug, and interpret their own analyses — applied to early postpartum depression risk (ClinPreAI) and pediatric diabetes clinical reasoning, benchmarked against classical ML and deep learning.
Extraction: LLM consensus pipelines that pull treatment-response phenotypes from clinical notes for rare disease research.
Privacy: evaluating LLMs for clinical-note de-identification, including a new category of context-dependent privacy risk (“institutionally-situated PHI”).
Foundation models: contributing to TEDDY, a generative pediatric EHR foundation model trained on data from millions of children.

Underneath it all is data engineering: large-scale PySpark pipelines over standardized EHR data (OMOP CDM, Epic Clarity) on Palantir Foundry and AWS.
Daniel is also an AI Developer and Research Design Intern at Peraton, where he builds LLM and multi-agent software and designs controlled experiments on how system design choices affect performance and reliability.
His path started in physics and mathematics at the University of Houston (B.S., magna cum laude, 2022), then NASA Ames and Johnson Space Center — radiation biology modeling and NLP for engineering failure analysis — with theoretical superconductivity research published in Physical Review B. That background shapes how he works: careful experimental design, rigorous evaluation, systems built to be trusted.
An NSF Graduate Research Fellow and NLM Fellow, Daniel has received Baylor’s Dean’s Award of Excellence and an Outstanding TA award. His work has been disseminated through peer-reviewed publications and 20+ conference presentations.
